This relatively low annual reproductive output is typical for a large arctic-breeding seabird. Neonate Pomarine jaegers emerge from the egg after an incubation period of approximately 26 days [ab = approximately 26 days], a figure recorded when eggs are maintained at a constant temperature of 36 °C [T = 36 °C] in artificial incubators. Immediately following hatching, the chick's initial wet weight is approximately 66 grams [Ww0 = approximately 66 grams], representing a substantial investment of maternal resources into a single offspring.

Fledging represents a major developmental milestone for the rapidly growing nestling. This degree of sexual size dimorphism is moderate among the Stercorariidae and likely reflects differing selective pressures related to territorial defense and foraging strategies during the breeding season.
